newsitem.title: UK: Britain to change telephone numbers again.
newsitem.headline: Britain to change telephone numbers again.

text.p: British regulator the Office of Telecommunications (Oftel) said on Tuesday that telephone prefixes, including those for London, would be changed to allow for billions of new numbers.

The changes come less than two years after a previous upheaval designed to cope with the same problem of number shortages, and will involve reuniting the current London codes of 0171 and 0181 under a single new code, 020.
Oftel Director General Don Cruickshank said the move would create a more meaningful plan for numbers, one designed to meet customers' needs for the 21st century.

"The new plan will be robust, flexible enough to meet new demands and will ensure that the UK maintains its place at the forefront of world telecommunications. In short, it is designed to be future-proof," Cruickshank said in a statement.
A range of numbers with the prefix 05 will be reserved for corporate use, allowing businesses to adopt a corporate identifier instead of having different numbers at different sites.
Mobile, paging and personal numbers are set to take the prefix 07 by 2001, special freephone and local rate services will have the prefix 08, and premium rate numbers will adopt 090 by the year 1999.

Aside from London, Portsmouth and Southampton, Cardiff and Northern Ireland are all to be given new prefixes starting with 02. Further 02 numbers will be created as they are needed, and 03 is also being reserved for future use in geographically distinct areas. The 04 and 06 ranges are being kept for future developments.
